historical_record.description: The Sharon Building went up at 300 Bowling Green Drive as a canteen for women and children, and is now a community art centre. One of the few Richardsonian Romanesque buildings in the city and the only local example with rough-hewn stone walls, it is City Landmark No. 124.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 124, Sharon Building.

Built to designs by Percy & Hamilton, with money William Sharon, the Comstock financier, left to the city, as the children's house and restaurant of the park's children's playground — with the carousel, the first public children's playground west of the Mississippi. It is a rare Victorian Romanesque building in sandstone; after 1906 it was rebuilt without its slate and copper roof.

On the Landmarks Preservation Advisory Board's recommendation, the City Planning Commission proposed, 4-1, that the Board of Supervisors designate the Sharon Building in Golden Gate Park a city landmark (Resolution 8752).
